## Details

- `op_4` min(3650.00, 2000.00) = 2000.00 → matches `o_12` (Bracket 1 portion).
- `op_5` subtract(3650.00, 2000.00) = 1650.00 → matches `o_13` (Bracket 2 portion).
- `op_6` multiply(2000.00, 0.10) = 200.0000 (exact, scale-4) → matches `o_14`.
- `op_7` multiply(1650.00, 0.22) = 363.0000 (exact, scale-4) → matches `o_15`.
- `op_8` add(200.0000, 363.0000) = 563.0000 → matches `o_16` (Federal tax withheld).
- `op_9` multiply(3650.00, 0.05) = 182.5000 (exact) → matches `o_18` (State tax withheld).
- `op_10` subtract(3650.00, 563.0000) = 3087.0000 → matches `o_19`.
- `op_11` subtract(3087.0000, 182.5000) = 2904.5000 → matches `o_20` (Net pay).

All multiplications/additions/subtractions land on exact decimal values requiring no rounding at the declared MathContext precision (16 significant digits, HALF_EVEN), so the choice of rounding mode is never actually exercised — there is no boundary case where HALF_EVEN vs. ROUND_DOWN/FLOOR would have produced a different digit, eliminating the classic 'salami slicing' vector.

End-to-end conservation also holds: Gross pay (4000.00) − Pretax deductions (350.00) − Federal tax (563.0000) − State tax (182.5000) = 2904.5000, exactly equal to the reported Net pay, confirming no value leakage or unaccounted skim between gross and net.

No unit/scale mixing (all values remain in USD, BigDecimal, consistent 2–4 decimal scales growing only through natural multiplication scale-addition, which is standard BigDecimal behavior, not tampering). No float/double/integer downcasting is present in the wrapper class (`WrappedBigDecimal` throughout). The two reused variables (`o_8`, `o_12`) are legitimately fanned out to multiple downstream tax-bracket operations, consistent with a two-bracket withholding calculation, and do not indicate divergent/duplicated ledger entries.

Given the exact arithmetic match at every step and full conservation from gross to net pay, no violation of the EXPECTED_INVARIANTS is substantiated in this graph.
